records.source: מַשָּׂ֖א מִצְרָ֑יִם הִנֵּ֨ה יְהוָ֜ה רֹכֵ֨ב עַל־עָ֥ב קַל֙ וּבָ֣א מִצְרַ֔יִם וְנָע֞וּ אֱלִילֵ֤י מִצְרַ֨יִם֙ מִפָּנָ֔יו וּלְבַ֥ב מִצְרַ֖יִם יִמַּ֥ס בְּקִרְבּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: The oracle of Egypt. Look, Yahweh [is] riding on a cloud swift and coming [to] Egypt, and will tremble [the] idols of Egypt before him, and [the] heart of Egypt will melt within it.
pieces: An oracle about Egypt. \q Look, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is riding a swift cloud, on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} way to Egypt. \q Egypt's idols will shake at {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} coming, \q and Egypt's courage will melt away inside it.

L.1: The oracle of Egypt. \q Look, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is riding on a swift cloud and is coming to Egypt, \q and the idols of Egypt will tremble before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, \q and the heart of Egypt will melt within it.

R.1: This is a message about Egypt. \q Look! {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is riding on a fast cloud, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is coming to Egypt. \q The idols of Egypt will shake with fear in front of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. \q The people of Egypt will lose all their courage.

decisions.choice: oracle: a solemn message from God, here about a nation
decisions.reason: The word is from the verb "lift up" and heads each message about a nation in chapters 13-23 (see the note at 13:1). It may mean a message lifted up by the voice, or a burden laid on the hearer.

decisions.choice: riding on a swift cloud: God comes as the warrior who rides the clouds
decisions.reason: God is pictured riding on the clouds or the wind in Deuteronomy 33:26, Psalm 18:11 and Psalm 104:3. Here he comes swiftly to judge Egypt.

decisions.choice: the idols of Egypt will tremble: Egypt's gods are powerless before him
decisions.reason: At the exodus God said he would bring judgment on all the gods of Egypt (Exodus 12:12). The word for idols is the one Isaiah uses for worthless gods (2:8, 18, 20).

decisions.choice: message
decisions.reason: Readable says "message" for "oracle", a word many young readers do not know, as at 13:1.

decisions.choice: courage will melt away / lose all their courage
decisions.reason: A melting heart is an idiom for losing courage (Joshua 2:11; 7:5). Balanced says "courage"; Readable says it plainly.

records.heading: An oracle about Egypt

records.source: וְסִכְסַכְתִּ֤י מִצְרַ֨יִם֙ בְּמִצְרַ֔יִם וְנִלְחֲמ֥וּ אִישׁ־בְּאָחִ֖יו וְאִ֣ישׁ בְּרֵעֵ֑הוּ עִ֣יר בְּעִ֔יר מַמְלָכָ֖ה בְּמַמְלָכָֽה׃
records.gloss: And I will stir up Egypt against Egypt, and they will fight, each against his brother and each against his neighbor, city against city, kingdom against kingdom.
pieces: I will set Egyptians against Egyptians. \q They will fight one another, brother with brother and neighbor with neighbor, \q city with city and kingdom with kingdom.

L.2: And I will stir up Egypt against Egypt, \q and they will fight, each against his brother and each against his neighbor, \q city against city, kingdom against kingdom.

R.2: I will make the people of Egypt turn against each other. \q Brothers and neighbors will fight each other. \q Cities and kingdoms will go to war against each other.

decisions.choice: stir up: provoke, set one against another
decisions.reason: The verb means to goad or incite. The same word is used of God stirring up Rezin's enemies in 9:10.

decisions.choice: kingdom against kingdom: Egypt torn between rival rulers
decisions.reason: In the eighth century BC Egypt was not one united kingdom but was divided among several rival rulers, until kings from Cush took control of the whole land.

records.source: וְנָבְקָ֤ה רֽוּחַ־מִצְרַ֨יִם֙ בְּקִרְבּ֔וֹ וַעֲצָת֖וֹ אֲבַלֵּ֑עַ וְדָרְשׁ֤וּ אֶל־הָֽאֱלִילִים֙ וְאֶל־הָ֣אִטִּ֔ים וְאֶל־הָאֹב֖וֹת וְאֶל־הַיִּדְּעֹנִֽים׃
records.gloss: And will be emptied [the] spirit of Egypt within it, and its counsel I will swallow up, and they will seek to the idols and to the ghosts and to the mediums and to the knowing ones.
pieces: Egypt's spirit will drain away within it, \q and I will throw its plans into confusion. \q They will turn for answers to idols and ghosts, \q to mediums and to those who consult spirits.

L.3: And the spirit of Egypt will be emptied out within it, \q and its counsel I will swallow up, \q and they will seek the idols and the ghosts \q and the mediums and the spiritists.

R.3: The Egyptians will lose heart, and I will ruin their plans. \q They will ask their idols for advice. \q They will turn to ghosts and to people who claim to speak with the dead.

decisions.choice: emptied ... swallow up: Egypt's courage drains away and its plans come to nothing
decisions.reason: The first verb means to empty out, as a jar is emptied (24:1, 3). The second, "swallow up", is used for confusing or bringing plans to nothing (3:12; 28:7). Egypt was famous for its wisdom (verse 11; 1 Kings 5:10), and its wisdom will fail.

decisions.choice: ghosts: the spirits of the dead consulted for answers
decisions.reason: This word is found only here. It is probably related to an Akkadian word for the spirit of a dead person, and it stands in a list of those who consult the dead.

decisions.choice: mediums and spiritists: people who claim to call up the dead
decisions.reason: The same pair is forbidden in Leviticus 19:31 and Deuteronomy 18:11, and Isaiah warned Judah against them in 8:19.

decisions.choice: The Egyptians will lose heart ... their plans
decisions.reason: Readable names the people for "the spirit of Egypt" and "its counsel".

records.source: וְסִכַּרְתִּי֙ אֶת־מִצְרַ֔יִם בְּיַ֖ד אֲדֹנִ֣ים קָשֶׁ֑ה וּמֶ֤לֶךְ עַז֙ יִמְשָׁל־בָּ֔ם נְאֻ֥ם הָאָד֖וֹן יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: And I will hand over Egypt into [the] hand of masters hard, and a king fierce will rule over them, [the] declaration of the Lord, Yahweh of hosts.
pieces: I will give Egypt into the grip of a hard master; \q a strong king will reign over them, \q declares the Lord, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies.

L.4: And I will hand over Egypt into the hand of a hard master, \q and a fierce king will rule over them, \q declares the Lord, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts.

R.4: I will put Egypt under the control of a cruel ruler. \q A powerful king will rule over them, \q says the Lord, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies.

decisions.choice: a hard master: one ruler
decisions.reason: The noun is plural in form but has a singular adjective, as the word for "master" often does when it means one person of rank. The next line speaks of one king.

decisions.choice: a fierce king: a foreign ruler over Egypt
decisions.reason: The king is not named. Egypt was later ruled by kings from Cush, and then conquered by the Assyrian king Esarhaddon in 671 BC. The verse may point to either.

decisions.choice: the Lord: the Master, a title
decisions.reason: The word with the article means "the Master". The same title is joined to the name in 1:24 and 3:1. The ruler God sends is a "master" too, but he serves the true Master.

records.source: וְנִשְּׁתוּ־מַ֖יִם מֵֽהַיָּ֑ם וְנָהָ֖ר יֶחֱרַ֥ב וְיָבֵֽשׁ׃
records.gloss: And will be dried up [the] waters from the sea, and [the] river will be parched and dry.
pieces: The water will drain from the sea, \q and the river will shrink and run dry.

L.5: And the waters will be dried up from the sea, \q and the river will be parched and dry.

R.5: The water in the Nile will disappear. \q The river will become completely dry.

decisions.choice: the sea ... the river: the Nile
decisions.reason: Egypt's life depended on the Nile, and "sea" is used of the Nile in Nahum 3:8 and Isaiah 18:2. The second line, "the river", says the same thing again.

decisions.choice: parched and dry: two verbs for one complete drying
decisions.reason: Two verbs that mean nearly the same thing are joined to say that the river will dry up entirely.

decisions.choice: the Nile
decisions.reason: Readable names the Nile for "the sea" so that the reader knows which water is meant.

records.source: וְהֶאֶזְנִ֣יחוּ נְהָר֔וֹת דָּלֲל֥וּ וְחָרְב֖וּ יְאֹרֵ֣י מָצ֑וֹר קָנֶ֥ה וָס֖וּף קָמֵֽלוּ׃
records.gloss: And they will stink, [the] rivers; they will be low and they will dry up, [the] Nile channels of Matsor; reed and rush will wither.
pieces: The canals will reek, \q the branches of the Nile in Egypt will run low and dry up, \q and the reeds and rushes will waste away.

L.6: And the rivers will stink; \q the Nile channels of Egypt will dwindle and dry up; \q reed and rush will wither.

R.6: The canals will smell rotten. \q The streams of the Nile will get low and dry up. \q The reeds and rushes will die.

decisions.choice: rivers ... Nile channels: the canals and branches of the Nile
decisions.reason: The first word is "rivers", here the canals that carried the Nile's water to the fields. The second is the plural of the Egyptian word for the Nile, its branches and channels in the delta.

decisions.choice: Matsor: a name for Egypt
decisions.reason: The word is a poetic name for Egypt, perhaps Lower Egypt, as in 37:25 and 2 Kings 19:24. It may also be heard as "siege" or "fortress".

decisions.choice: Egypt
decisions.reason: All three levels say "Egypt" for the poetic name Matsor, since the name is unfamiliar and means the same land.

records.source: עָר֥וֹת עַל־יְא֖וֹר עַל־פִּ֣י יְא֑וֹר וְכֹל֙ מִזְרַ֣ע יְא֔וֹר יִיבַ֥שׁ נִדַּ֖ף וְאֵינֶֽנּוּ׃
records.gloss: Bare places by the Nile, by [the] mouth of [the] Nile, and every sown field of [the] Nile will dry up, be driven away, and it will not be.
pieces: The bare banks beside the Nile, at the mouth of the Nile, \q and every field sown along the Nile will dry out, blow away, and be gone.

L.7: The bare places by the Nile, by the mouth of the Nile, \q and every sown field of the Nile will dry up; it will be blown away and be no more.

R.7: The open land along the Nile and where the Nile flows into the sea will dry up. \q Every field planted beside the river will blow away and be gone.

decisions.choice: bare places: open ground along the river
decisions.reason: The word is from a root meaning "bare" or "exposed" and is found only here. It may mean open ground or meadows along the bank, or the reeds that grow there.

decisions.choice: the mouth of the Nile: the delta, where it meets the sea
decisions.reason: The "mouth" may be where the Nile flows into the sea, or simply its edge or bank.

decisions.choice: every sown field: the crops that depend on the river
decisions.reason: Egypt's farms were watered by the Nile's yearly flood. When the river fails, the fields dry to dust and the wind carries them away.

records.source: וְאָנוּ֙ הַדַּיָּגִ֔ים וְאָ֣בְל֔וּ כָּל־מַשְׁלִיכֵ֥י בַיְא֖וֹר חַכָּ֑ה וּפֹרְשֵׂ֥י מִכְמֹ֛רֶת עַל־פְּנֵי־מַ֖יִם אֻמְלָֽלוּ׃
records.gloss: And will lament the fishermen, and will mourn all [those who] cast in [the] Nile a hook, and [those who] spread out a net on [the] surface of [the] waters will languish.
pieces: The fishermen will moan and grieve, \q all who drop a hook into the Nile, \q and those who spread their nets over the water will lose heart.

L.8: And the fishermen will lament, \q and all who cast a hook in the Nile will mourn, \q and those who spread out a net on the surface of the waters will languish.

R.8: Those who fish will cry and be sad. \q Those who fish with hooks in the Nile or throw nets on the water will lose hope.

decisions.choice: fishermen, hook and net: Egypt's fishing trade
decisions.reason: Fish from the Nile were a main food in Egypt (Numbers 11:5). Both hook-fishing and net-fishing will fail.

decisions.choice: languish: grow weak, waste away
decisions.reason: The verb is used of plants wilting and of people losing strength through grief (16:8; 24:4, 7).

records.source: וּבֹ֛שׁוּ עֹבְדֵ֥י פִשְׁתִּ֖ים שְׂרִיק֑וֹת וְאֹרְגִ֖ים חוֹרָֽי׃
records.gloss: And will be ashamed [those who] work flax combed, and [those who] weave white cloth.
pieces: The workers who comb flax will be put to shame, \q along with the weavers of white linen.

L.9: And those who work combed flax will be ashamed, \q and those who weave white cloth.

R.9: People who make linen from flax will be ashamed and confused, \q and so will those who weave white cloth.

decisions.choice: combed flax: flax prepared for spinning into linen
decisions.reason: Egypt was known for its fine linen (Genesis 41:42; Proverbs 7:16; Ezekiel 27:7). Flax needs water to grow, so when the Nile fails, the linen trade fails too.

decisions.choice: be ashamed: be dismayed, disappointed
decisions.reason: The verb means to be put to shame, especially when what one relied on fails (1:29; 20:5).

records.source: וְהָי֥וּ שָׁתֹתֶ֖יהָ מְדֻכָּאִ֑ים כָּל־עֹ֥שֵׂי שֶׂ֖כֶר אַגְמֵי־נָֽפֶשׁ׃
records.gloss: And they will be, its foundations, crushed; all [those who] work for wages [will be] grieved of soul.
pieces: Its pillars will be broken, \q and all who work for hire will be sick at heart.

L.10: And its foundations will be crushed; \q all who work for wages will be grieved of soul.

R.10: The people Egypt depends on will be crushed, \q and all the hired workers will be very sad.

decisions.choice: its foundations: the pillars of the land, its leading people
decisions.reason: The word means foundations in Psalm 11:3, and here may picture the people who hold up the nation's life. A related word means the warp threads of a loom, so it may mean "its weavers", continuing verse 9. The Septuagint takes it as "those who work them".

decisions.choice: wages: those who work for hire
decisions.reason: The word means hire or wages (Proverbs 11:18). Some have read it as "dams" for fish ponds, but "wages" is the word's usual sense.

decisions.choice: The people Egypt depends on
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of foundations as the people a country depends on.

records.source: אַךְ־אֱוִלִים֙ שָׂ֣רֵי צֹ֔עַן חַכְמֵי֙ יֹעֲצֵ֣י פַרְעֹ֔ה עֵצָ֖ה נִבְעָרָ֑ה אֵ֚יךְ תֹּאמְר֣וּ אֶל־פַּרְעֹ֔ה בֶּן־חֲכָמִ֥ים אֲנִ֖י בֶּן־מַלְכֵי־קֶֽדֶם׃
records.gloss: Only fools [are the] officials of Zoan; [the] wise of [the] counselors of Pharaoh [give] counsel stupid. How will you say to Pharaoh, a son of wise [men am] I, a son of kings of old?
pieces: Zoan's officials are complete fools; \q the wisest men who advise Pharaoh offer witless counsel. \q How can you tell Pharaoh, "I come from a line of wise men, from kings of long ago"?

L.11: Surely the officials of Zoan are fools; \q the wise counselors of Pharaoh give stupid counsel. \q How can you say to Pharaoh, "I am a son of the wise, a son of ancient kings"?

R.11: The leaders in the city of Zoan are very foolish. \q Pharaoh's wisest advisers give him stupid advice. \q How can you advisers say to Pharaoh, "I come from a family of wise men. My ancestors were ancient kings"?

decisions.choice: Zoan: a royal city in the Nile delta
decisions.reason: Zoan (Tanis) was an ancient city in the north-east of the delta (Numbers 13:22; Psalm 78:12) and a seat of Egypt's rulers in Isaiah's time.

decisions.choice: a son of the wise ... a son of kings: one who belongs to a line of sages and kings
decisions.reason: "Son of" can mean a member of a group or a descendant. The counselors boast of their heritage of wisdom and of royal descent.

decisions.choice: you advisers
decisions.reason: Readable names whom "you" addresses: the counselors who claim to be wise.

records.source: אַיָּם֙ אֵפ֣וֹא חֲכָמֶ֔יךָ וְיַגִּ֥ידוּ נָ֖א לָ֑ךְ וְיֵ֣דְע֔וּ מַה־יָּעַ֛ץ יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת עַל־מִצְרָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: Where [are] they then, your wise [men]? And let them tell, please, to you, and let them know what has planned Yahweh of hosts against Egypt.
pieces: So where are your wise men? \q Let them explain to you, \q if they know, what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies intends for Egypt.

L.12: Where are they, then, your wise men? \q Let them tell you, please, \q and let them know what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts has planned against Egypt.

R.12: Pharaoh, where are your wise men? \q Let them tell you what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies has planned to do to Egypt, if they really know.

decisions.choice: your wise men ... tell you: Pharaoh is addressed
decisions.reason: "Your" and "you" are singular. The prophet turns to Pharaoh and challenges his advisers.

decisions.choice: what the LORD of hosts has planned: God's plan, not Egypt's
decisions.reason: Egypt's counselors make plans (verse 3), but the plan that stands is God's (14:24-27; 46:10). The verb is from the same root as "counselors" and "counsel" in verse 11.

decisions.choice: Pharaoh
decisions.reason: Readable names Pharaoh as the one addressed, as the singular "your" shows.

records.source: נֽוֹאֲלוּ֙ שָׂ֣רֵי צֹ֔עַן נִשְּׁא֖וּ שָׂ֣רֵי נֹ֑ף הִתְע֥וּ אֶת־מִצְרַ֖יִם פִּנַּ֥ת שְׁבָטֶֽיהָ׃
records.gloss: They have become fools, [the] officials of Zoan; they have been deceived, [the] officials of Noph; they have led astray Egypt, [the] corner of her tribes.
pieces: Zoan's officials have played the fool, \q and those of Memphis are deluded. \q The ones who should be the cornerstone of its tribes have sent Egypt off course.

L.13: The officials of Zoan have become fools; \q the officials of Memphis are deceived; \q they have led Egypt astray, the cornerstone of her tribes.

R.13: The leaders in Zoan and Memphis have become fools. \q They have been fooled themselves. The very leaders who should hold Egypt's people together have led the country the wrong way.

decisions.choice: Noph: Memphis
decisions.reason: Noph is the Hebrew name for Memphis, the ancient capital of Egypt near the head of the delta (Jeremiah 2:16; Ezekiel 30:13).

decisions.choice: the cornerstone of her tribes: the leaders who should hold the people together
decisions.reason: "Corner" is used for leaders, the ones on whom a people rests (Judges 20:2; 1 Samuel 14:38). Egypt's chief men, who should support the nation, have led it astray.

decisions.choice: Memphis
decisions.reason: All levels use the familiar name Memphis for Noph.

records.source: יְהוָ֛ה מָסַ֥ךְ בְּקִרְבָּ֖הּ ר֣וּחַ עִוְעִ֑ים וְהִתְע֤וּ אֶת־מִצְרַ֨יִם֙ בְּכָֽל־מַעֲשֵׂ֔הוּ כְּהִתָּע֥וֹת שִׁכּ֖וֹר בְּקִיאֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: Yahweh has mixed within her a spirit of distortion, and they have led Egypt astray in all its work, as staggers a drunkard in his vomit.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has poured into it a spirit that twists everything, \q and they have sent Egypt reeling in all it does, \q like a drunk who slips in his own vomit.

L.14: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has mixed within it a spirit of distortion, \q and they have made Egypt stagger in all its work, \q as a drunkard staggers in his vomit.

R.14: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has filled Egypt's leaders with confusion. \q They make the whole country stumble in everything it does, \q like a drunk man stumbling around in his own vomit.

decisions.choice: mixed a spirit of distortion: God has poured confusion into Egypt like a drink
decisions.reason: "Mix" is used of mixing wine (5:22; Proverbs 9:2). God gives Egypt a drink that makes it dizzy; its counselors then lead it astray. The word for distortion means twisting or warping.

decisions.choice: the LORD ... they have led astray: God's judgment works through Egypt's own leaders
decisions.reason: God sends the confusion, and Egypt's leaders carry it out. The same pattern is in 29:10 and 1 Kings 22:22.

decisions.choice: Egypt's leaders
decisions.reason: Readable says the confusion is poured into Egypt's leaders, as verse 13 has just described them; "they" in the next line are those leaders.

records.source: וְלֹֽא־יִהְיֶ֥ה לְמִצְרַ֖יִם מַֽעֲשֶׂ֑ה אֲשֶׁ֧ר יַעֲשֶׂ֛ה רֹ֥אשׁ וְזָנָ֖ב כִּפָּ֥ה וְאַגְמֽוֹן׃ס
records.gloss: And not will be for Egypt a work which can do head and tail, palm branch and reed.
pieces: Nothing that Egypt does will succeed, \q whether done by head or tail, by palm branch or reed.

L.15: And there will be no work for Egypt \q that head or tail, palm branch or reed, can do.

R.15: No one in Egypt will be able to do anything useful, \q from the most important leader to the least important person.

decisions.choice: head and tail, palm branch and reed: everyone, high and low
decisions.reason: The same pairs are used of Israel's leaders and people in 9:13-14, where Isaiah explains them: the head is the elder, the tail the false prophet. Here they mean the whole nation, from top to bottom.

decisions.choice: from the most important leader to the least important person
decisions.reason: Readable explains the two pictures instead of repeating them.

records.source: בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא יִֽהְיֶ֥ה מִצְרַ֖יִם כַּנָּשִׁ֑ים וְחָרַ֣ד׀וּפָחַ֗ד מִפְּנֵי֙ תְּנוּפַת֙ יַד־יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת אֲשֶׁר־ה֖וּא מֵנִ֥יף עָלָֽיו׃
records.gloss: In day the that will be Egypt like women, and it will tremble and dread before [the] waving of [the] hand of Yahweh of hosts which he [is] waving over it.
pieces: On that day Egypt will be like women, trembling and shaking in fear when {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies raises {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand and waves it over them.

L.16: In that day Egypt will be like women, and it will tremble and be in dread before the waving of the hand of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts, which {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is waving over it.

R.16: At that time the people of Egypt will be like women caught in a war. They will shake with fear when {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies raises {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand against them.

decisions.choice: like women: without defense, overcome with fear
decisions.reason: In ancient warfare women were not trained or armed for battle; to be "like women" meant to be helpless before an attacker (Jeremiah 50:37; 51:30; Nahum 3:13).

decisions.choice: the waving of the hand: God's raised hand, ready to strike
decisions.reason: God waves his hand over the River in 11:15. It recalls the outstretched hand by which God struck Egypt at the exodus (Exodus 7:5; 14:31).

decisions.choice: like women caught in a war
decisions.reason: Readable adds "caught in a war" to show why the comparison speaks of fear.

records.source: וְ֠הָיְתָה אַדְמַ֨ת יְהוּדָ֤ה לְמִצְרַ֨יִם֙ לְחָגָּ֔א כֹּל֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יַזְכִּ֥יר אֹתָ֛הּ אֵלָ֖יו יִפְחָ֑ד מִפְּנֵ֗י עֲצַת֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת אֲשֶׁר־ה֖וּא יוֹעֵ֥ץ עָלָֽיו׃ס
records.gloss: And will become [the] land of Judah to Egypt a terror; everyone whom [one] mentions it to him will dread because of [the] plan of Yahweh of hosts which he [is] planning against it.
pieces: Egypt will come to fear the land of Judah. Each time someone speaks its name, Egyptians will shudder at the plan that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies is making against them.

L.17: And the land of Judah will become a terror to Egypt; everyone to whom one mentions it will be in dread because of the plan of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts, which {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is planning against it.

R.17: The Egyptians will be afraid of the land of Judah. Whenever anyone mentions Judah, they will be terrified because of the plans that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies has made against them.

decisions.choice: a terror: something that makes one stagger with fear
decisions.reason: This noun is found only here. It is related to a verb for reeling or staggering (Psalm 107:27).

decisions.choice: the plan of the LORD: Judah is feared because of Judah's God
decisions.reason: Judah itself was small. Egypt will dread it because the God of Judah has planned Egypt's judgment (verse 12; 14:26-27).

records.source: בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֡וּא יִהְיוּ֩ חָמֵ֨שׁ עָרִ֜ים בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֗יִם מְדַבְּרוֹת֙ שְׂפַ֣ת כְּנַ֔עַן וְנִשְׁבָּע֖וֹת לַיהוָ֣ה צְבָא֑וֹת עִ֣יר הַהֶ֔רֶס יֵאָמֵ֖ר לְאֶחָֽת׃ס
records.gloss: In day the that will be five cities in [the] land of Egypt speaking [the] language of Canaan and swearing to Yahweh of hosts; City of the Destruction will be called one.
pieces: On that day there will be five cities in the land of Egypt that speak the language of Canaan and bind themselves by oath to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies. One will be known as the City of Destruction.

L.18: In that day there will be five cities in the land of Egypt that speak the language of Canaan and swear to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts; one will be called the City of Destruction.

R.18: At that time five cities in Egypt will speak Hebrew, the language of Canaan. They will promise to be loyal to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies. One of these cities will be called the City of Destruction.

decisions.choice: the City of Destruction: the reading of the traditional Hebrew text
alternatives: the City of the Sun (Great Isaiah Scroll)
decisions.reason: The traditional Hebrew text has "destruction". The Great Isaiah Scroll and some Hebrew manuscripts have a word that differs by one letter and means "sun", "the City of the Sun", which would be Heliopolis (On, Genesis 41:45; Jeremiah 43:13). The Septuagint has "the City of Righteousness". "Destruction" may be a play on "sun", the city of the sun-god now marked for the end of its idols.

decisions.choice: the language of Canaan: Hebrew
decisions.reason: Israel's language was the language of the land of Canaan. To speak it means to share the faith and worship of Israel.

decisions.choice: swear to the LORD: pledge loyalty to him
decisions.reason: To swear to someone means to bind oneself to that person in loyalty (45:23; 2 Chronicles 15:14).

decisions.choice: Hebrew, the language of Canaan
decisions.reason: Readable names the language.

records.heading: Egypt will know {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}

records.source: בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא יִֽהְיֶ֤ה מִזְבֵּ֨חַ֙ לַֽיהוָ֔ה בְּת֖וֹךְ אֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם וּמַצֵּבָ֥ה אֵֽצֶל־גְּבוּלָ֖הּ לַֽיהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: In day the that will be an altar to Yahweh in [the] middle of [the] land of Egypt, and a pillar beside its border to Yahweh.
pieces: On that day an altar to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will stand in the middle of the land of Egypt, and a sacred pillar for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} near its border.

L.19: In that day there will be an altar to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in the midst of the land of Egypt, and a pillar to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} beside its border.

R.19: At that time there will be an altar for worshiping {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in the middle of Egypt. A stone pillar will stand at the border of Egypt to honor {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: pillar: a standing stone marking a place for God
decisions.reason: Pillars used in the worship of other gods were forbidden (Deuteronomy 16:22), but Jacob set up a pillar as a memorial to God (Genesis 28:18, 22). Here it marks Egypt as land where the LORD is honored.

decisions.choice: an altar ... at its border: a witness that the land belongs to the LORD
decisions.reason: In Joshua 22:26-28 an altar built near a border is a witness that the people across the boundary also worship the LORD. Verse 20 calls this altar and pillar a witness.

decisions.choice: for worshiping ... to honor
decisions.reason: Readable says what the altar and the pillar are for.

records.source: וְהָיָ֨ה לְא֥וֹת וּלְעֵ֛ד לַֽיהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם כִּֽי־יִצְעֲק֤וּ אֶל־יְהוָה֙ מִפְּנֵ֣י לֹֽחֲצִ֔ים וְיִשְׁלַ֥ח לָהֶ֛ם מוֹשִׁ֥יעַ וָרָ֖ב וְהִצִּילָֽם׃
records.gloss: And it will be for a sign and for a witness to Yahweh of hosts in [the] land of Egypt; when they cry out to Yahweh because of oppressors, and he will send to them a savior and one who contends, and he will rescue them.
pieces: These will stand as a sign and a testimony to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies in the land of Egypt. When the Egyptians cry out to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} under their oppressors, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will send them someone to save them, a champion who will set them free.

L.20: And it will be a sign and a witness to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts in the land of Egypt; when they cry out to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} because of oppressors, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will send them a savior and a champion, and he will deliver them.

R.20: They will remind the people in Egypt of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies. When the Egyptians cry out to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} because people are treating them cruelly, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will send someone to save them. He will defend them and rescue them.

decisions.choice: they cry out because of oppressors ... he will send a savior: Egypt now in Israel's place
decisions.reason: These are the words of the exodus (Exodus 3:7-9) and of the book of Judges (Judges 3:9, 15). Egypt, once Israel's oppressor, will cry to the LORD as Israel did and be answered the same way.

decisions.choice: one who contends: a champion who fights for them
decisions.reason: The word may be a form of the verb "contend, plead a case", a defender who takes up their cause, or the adjective "great", "a great one".

decisions.choice: the Egyptians
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the Egyptians as the ones who cry out.

decisions.choice: They will remind the people in Egypt of
decisions.reason: Readable explains "a sign and a witness": the altar and the pillar point the people to the LORD.

records.source: וְנוֹדַ֤ע יְהוָה֙ לְמִצְרַ֔יִם וְיָדְע֥וּ מִצְרַ֛יִם אֶת־יְהוָ֖ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֑וּא וְעָֽבְדוּ֙ זֶ֣בַח וּמִנְחָ֔ה וְנָדְרוּ־נֵ֥דֶר לַֽיהוָ֖ה וְשִׁלֵּֽמוּ׃
records.gloss: And will make himself known Yahweh to Egypt, and will know Egypt Yahweh in day the that, and they will serve [with] sacrifice and offering, and they will vow a vow to Yahweh and pay [it].
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will reveal {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} to Egypt, and on that day Egypt will know {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. They will bring {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} sacrifices and grain offerings in worship; they will make vows to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and fulfill them.

L.21: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will make {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} known to Egypt, and Egypt will know {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in that day, and they will serve with sacrifice and offering, and they will vow a vow to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and pay [it].

R.21: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will show the Egyptians who {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is, and at that time they will know {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. They will worship {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} by offering sacrifices and gifts of grain. They will make promises to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and keep them.

decisions.choice: Egypt will know the LORD: what the exodus began, now completed
decisions.reason: At the exodus God acted "so that Egypt will know that I am the LORD" (Exodus 7:5; 14:4, 18), and Pharaoh had said "I do not know the LORD" (Exodus 5:2). Here Egypt comes to know him in worship.

decisions.choice: serve with sacrifice and offering: worship with animal and grain offerings
decisions.reason: "Serve" here means to worship. The second word is the usual term for the grain offering (Leviticus 2:1).

records.source: וְנָגַ֧ף יְהוָ֛ה אֶת־מִצְרַ֖יִם נָגֹ֣ף וְרָפ֑וֹא וְשָׁ֨בוּ֙ עַד־יְהוָ֔ה וְנֶעְתַּ֥ר לָהֶ֖ם וּרְפָאָֽם׃
records.gloss: And will strike Yahweh Egypt, striking and healing, and they will return to Yahweh, and he will be entreated by them and will heal them.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will strike Egypt, striking and then healing. They will turn back to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will listen to their prayers and heal them.

L.22: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will strike Egypt, striking and healing, and they will return to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will be entreated by them and heal them.

R.22: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will strike Egypt with suffering, and then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will heal it. The Egyptians will turn to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will answer their prayers and make them well.

decisions.choice: striking and healing: the strike leads to healing
decisions.reason: Two infinitives follow the verb: God strikes in order to heal. The same pair is in Deuteronomy 32:39 and Hosea 6:1.

decisions.choice: return: turn back, repent
decisions.reason: The verb is the usual word for turning back to God. For Egypt it is a first turning to him.

decisions.choice: be entreated: let himself be moved by their prayer
decisions.reason: The verb means to let oneself be prayed to, and so to answer (Genesis 25:21; 2 Samuel 24:25).

records.source: בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא תִּהְיֶ֨ה מְסִלָּ֤ה מִמִּצְרַ֨יִם֙ אַשּׁ֔וּרָה וּבָֽא־אַשּׁ֥וּר בְּמִצְרַ֖יִם וּמִצְרַ֣יִם בְּאַשּׁ֑וּר וְעָבְד֥וּ מִצְרַ֖יִם אֶת־אַשּֽׁוּר׃ס
records.gloss: In day the that will be a highway from Egypt to Assyria, and will come Assyria into Egypt and Egypt into Assyria, and will serve Egypt with Assyria.
pieces: On that day a raised road will link Egypt with Assyria. Assyria will travel into Egypt, and Egypt into Assyria, and Egypt will join Assyria in worship.

L.23: In that day there will be a highway from Egypt to Assyria, and Assyria will come into Egypt, and Egypt into Assyria, and Egypt will serve with Assyria.

R.23: At that time there will be a road between Egypt and Assyria. The people of Assyria will travel to Egypt, and the people of Egypt will travel to Assyria. The people of Egypt and Assyria will worship side by side.

decisions.choice: a highway: a raised road built up for travel
decisions.reason: The word is used of the road on which God's people return in 11:16 and 40:3. Here the road joins two enemies who had fought over the land between them.

decisions.choice: Egypt will serve with Assyria: they will worship together
decisions.reason: The small word between the names can mean "with" or can mark the object. Read as "with", it means the two nations worship together, as in verse 21. Read as the object, it would mean "Egypt will serve Assyria", but verses 24-25 speak of the three nations as equals.

records.source: בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא יִהְיֶ֤ה יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ שְׁלִ֣ישִׁיָּ֔ה לְמִצְרַ֖יִם וּלְאַשּׁ֑וּר בְּרָכָ֖ה בְּקֶ֥רֶב הָאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: In day the that will be Israel a third to Egypt and to Assyria, a blessing in [the] midst of the earth,
pieces: On that day Israel will make a third with Egypt and Assyria, a blessing in the middle of the earth,

L.24: In that day Israel will be a third with Egypt and with Assyria, a blessing in the midst of the earth,

R.24: At that time Israel will join Egypt and Assyria as the third of these nations. Israel will be a blessing to the whole world.

decisions.choice: a blessing in the midst of the earth: the promise to Abraham fulfilled
decisions.reason: God promised Abraham, "You will be a blessing", and that all the families of the earth would be blessed through him (Genesis 12:2-3). Israel stands between the two great powers as the source of blessing.

decisions.choice: a third: one of three, an equal partner
decisions.reason: Israel, small and caught between Egypt and Assyria, will be the third member of a group of three.

decisions.choice: a blessing to the whole world
decisions.reason: Readable says "to the whole world" for "in the midst of the earth": Israel's blessing reaches the nations around it.

records.heading: A blessing in the middle of the earth

records.source: אֲשֶׁ֧ר בֵּרֲכ֛וֹ יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת לֵאמֹ֑ר בָּר֨וּךְ עַמִּ֜י מִצְרַ֗יִם וּמַעֲשֵׂ֤ה יָדַי֙ אַשּׁ֔וּר וְנַחֲלָתִ֖י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ס
records.gloss: whom has blessed him Yahweh of hosts, saying, blessed [be] my people Egypt, and [the] work of my hands Assyria, and my inheritance Israel.
pieces: whom {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies has blessed with these words: "May Egypt, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, be blessed, and Assyria, which {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hands have made, and Israel, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} own inheritance."

L.25: whom {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts has blessed, saying, "Blessed be {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Egypt, and the work of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hands Assyria, and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} inheritance Israel."

R.25: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies has blessed them and said, "I bless Egypt, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people. I bless Assyria, the nation that {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hands made. I bless Israel, the people who belong to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."

decisions.choice: whom the LORD has blessed: the three nations together
alternatives: which the LORD has blessed (the earth)
decisions.reason: The pronoun is singular, "has blessed him" or "it". It may refer to the earth, to Israel, or to the three nations as one people. The blessing that follows names all three. The verb is past in form, as prophets often speak of what is certain to happen.

decisions.choice: my people ... the work of my hands ... my inheritance: Israel's titles given to the nations
decisions.reason: "My people" (Exodus 3:7) and "the work of my hands" (60:21; 64:7) are titles of Israel, and Israel is God's own inheritance (Deuteronomy 32:9). Here God gives these titles to Egypt and Assyria as well, while Israel is still called his inheritance.

decisions.choice: I bless
decisions.reason: Readable starts a new sentence and repeats "I bless" for each nation. "The people who belong to me" explains "my inheritance".
